title: hotfix: stabilize-slo-enforcer-backoff-regional-failover-load-shedding
author: Aisha Raman
description:
Fixes an SLO enforcer backoff ordering bug that caused thrashing during regional failover + aggressive load-shedding. Root cause: concurrent backoff state updates in backoff_manager allowed stale timers to reset effective cooldown, leading to rapid open/close cycles and excessive shedding. This hotfix introduces stronger ordering guarantees, replaces an ad-hoc timestamp comparison with a compare-and-swap (CAS) for backoff state, and adds a small exponential backoff floor to prevent sub-millisecond cooldowns. Also includes a metric to track 'backoff_state_revocations' to help diagnose future regressions.

Why: Several incidents in the last 24 hours (linked Linear ENG-3421) showed regional failover triggered while capacity was constrained; SLO enforcer thrashing amplified the outage and caused client-visible 503s. This change reduces oscillation risk and makes the enforcer more robust under failover conditions.

What I changed (high level): updated backoff manager to use atomic CAS for state transitions; added an explicit cooldown floor and jitter; guarded the regional failover code path to prefer soft-fallback before full shed; added unit tests and an integration test that reproduces the regression; added a Prometheus metric and a small runbook note.

Testing: unit tests added for backoff ordering, integration test simulates regional failover under load in CI, manual verification on staging with chaos injection. CI initially failed due to a flaky timing assertion which was replaced with a deterministic fixture.

Rollout plan: immediate squash-and-merge to main, canary 5% in control plane for 10 minutes, then 25% for 30 minutes, then full. If errors increase, rollback to previous main and follow runbook.

Checklist:
- [x] Add CAS-based state transitions
- [x] Add cooldown floor + jitter
- [x] Add metric backoff_state_revocations
- [x] Add unit + integration tests
- [x] Update runbook docs
- [x] CI green after rerun
